spells.name: Affect Normal Fires

fields.Area: One normal fire up to 3′ diameter

effect: Dim an ordinary fire to match-like light, or brighten it to the illumination of light.
conditions: Dimming halves fuel consumption; brightening doubles it.
exceptions: Heat output is unchanged.

spells.name: Enlarge

fields.Material: Pinch of powdered iron

effect: Living targets grow 20% per caster level, up to 200% additional size; objects grow 10% per level, up to 100% additional size.
Weight, mass and strength change with the enlargement.
conditions: Initial affected volume cannot exceed 10 cubic feet of living matter or 5 cubic feet of nonliving matter per level.
The caster must see the target.
exceptions: Magical properties do not increase: a larger magic weapon retains its existing enchantment.
Reverse: reduce shrinks in the same proportions or counters enlargement.

spells.name: Erase

fields.Area: One scroll or two facing pages

effect: Remove magical or mundane writing from suitable paper, parchment or similar surfaces.
conditions: Success is 50% plus 2% per caster level for magical writing, or 50% plus 4% per level for ordinary writing.
A percentile roll exceeding that chance fails.
exceptions: Explosive runes and symbol cannot be erased this way.

spells.name: Find Familiar

fields.Saving throw: Special; summoned special familiars may resist
fields.Material: Brass brazier with charcoal, 100 gp of incense, herbs including basil/savory/catnip, and fat

effect: Call a familiar that can share senses, converse and serve as scout or guard; the caster cannot choose its kind.
A normal familiar has 2–4 HP and AC 7; while within 12″, its HP are added to its master's total.
conditions: The ritual may be attempted only once a year, and can produce no familiar.
Continue the incantation until the familiar arrives or the casting period ends.
The DM secretly determines the result.
exceptions: If the familiar dies, its master permanently loses twice the familiar's HP.
Special familiars have additional creature-specific rules; a successful resistance save leaves no familiar available that year.

Normal familiar table on d20: 1–4 black cat, 5–6 crow, 7–8 hawk, 9–10 screech owl, 11–12 toad, 13–14 weasel, 15 special, 16–20 no familiar. The printed adjustment subtracts 1 for each three caster levels and specifies a subsequent d16 roll in the stated circumstance.

For a special familiar, chaotic evil/neutral chaotic yields quasit; chaotic good/neutral good pseudo-dragon; lawful good/neutral lawful brownie; lawful evil/neutral evil imp. Consult the referenced Monster Manual for special-familiar powers.

spells.name: Identify

fields.Material: Pearl worth at least 100 gp and owl feather steeped in wine; drink infusion and swallow a live miniature carp

effect: Examine one potential property each segment, with a 15% + 5% per caster-level chance to reach that step.
A successful secret save versus magic reveals the property; missing by one yields false information, and a worse failure reveals nothing.
conditions: Handle or wear the item in its normal manner, accepting its ordinary consequences.
Begin examining within one hour per caster level after discovery, before later handling obscures the impressions.
Afterward lose 8 Constitution temporarily; regain one point per six turns of rest. Falling below Constitution 3 causes unconsciousness until full recovery 24 hours later.
exceptions: Exact attack/damage bonuses are not disclosed; charge estimates can be 25% above or below the actual amount.
Powdering a luckstone into the infusion adds 25% to the information chance and +4 to the saves.

spells.name: Nystul'S Magic Aura

fields.Area: One item weighing at most 50 gp/level
fields.Material: Small silk square passed over the item

effect: Give an item a misleading aura that registers to magic detection.
conditions: A detector who actually holds it may save versus magic to recognize the deception.
exceptions: Without that successful save the aura appears magical, but testing does not identify a real magical function.

spells.name: Protection from Evil

fields.Material: Powdered iron and silver used to trace the protective circle

effect: Evil attackers take −2 to hit the protected creature, which gains +2 on saving throws caused by their attacks.
The protective boundary bars bodily contact by enchanted, conjured or summoned creatures as described in the cleric version.
exceptions: Reverse: protection from good changes the alignment-based attack/save protection, while still excluding enchanted evil creatures.

spells.name: Push

fields.Material: Pinch of powdered brass blown from the palm

effect: Apply one foot-pound of force per caster level, moving small objects up to one foot away from the caster or toppling them when conditions permit.
An off-balance attacking creature that fails its save loses that round's attack; its weight cannot exceed 50 pounds per caster level.
conditions: Against a held object, a failed save lets the force subtract from its holder's to-hit chance or add to an opponent's relevant save.

spells.name: Ventriloquism

fields.Material: Small parchment cone

effect: Make a voice or a sound the caster can normally produce seem to originate elsewhere.
conditions: Speech must use a language the caster knows.
A hearer has a 10% chance per Intelligence point above 12 to recognize the trick.

spells.name: Write

fields.Material: Writing surface and rare ink costing at least 200 gp per bottle

effect: Attempt to copy a spell the caster cannot yet understand because of spell level or Intelligence.
conditions: Copying takes one hour per spell level; the caster is in a trance and can always be surprised.
The saving-throw modifier is +2 for a spell one level above current use and 0 for two levels above.
A failed save deals 1d4 damage per level of the copied spell and causes the same number of turns unconscious; this damage heals only 1–4 HP per day.
exceptions: The printed text gives a −1 per level penalty from three levels higher onward.

spells.name: Audible Glamer

fields.Material: Bit of wool or small lump of wax

effect: Create sounds at a chosen point that can stay put, approach or recede.
At caster level 3, maximum volume equals four people; each later level adds another four people's volume.
conditions: A creature that declares disbelief may save; success reduces the sound to nothing or a faint remnant.
exceptions: The sound can complement phantasmal force, which supplies no sound on its own.

spells.name: Continual Light

fields.Saving throw: None; targeted creature receives the inherited save

effect: Create near-daylight illumination in air or on an object or creature, lasting until countered or dispelled.
conditions: A successful save by a targeted creature puts the light about one foot behind it.
A successful casting on visual organs can blind the target.
exceptions: The magic-user version cannot be reversed by its caster.

spells.name: Darkness, 15' Radius

fields.Material: Bat fur and either a drop of pitch or a piece of coal

effect: Create darkness that blocks normal sight, infravision and ultravision.
exceptions: Ordinary and magical light do not illuminate it, except the listed light and continual light counters.
The text explicitly says light and darkness negate one another; it also lists continual light as an exception.

spells.name: Detect Evil
effect: Sense evil emanations from creatures or objects; the reverse detects good.
conditions: The detection path extends in the direction the caster faces.
exceptions: An ordinary hidden trap or unintelligent venomous creature does not register merely because it is dangerous.

spells.name: ESP

fields.Material: Copper piece

effect: Read a creature's surface thoughts, including simple instincts from lower-order minds.
The spell can reveal a mind beyond a door without necessarily identifying the creature.
conditions: Two feet of rock, two inches of non-lead metal, or even thin lead foil block the probe.
Undead and other beings without a mind recognizable to the spell are excluded.
exceptions: Gap: the paragraph uses both one-creature-per-turn and round-to-round probe timing; this needs source review.

spells.name: Fool's Gold

fields.Material: Powdered citrine (50 gp), amber (100 gp), topaz (500 gp), or oriental topaz (1,000 gp)

effect: Make copper coins or brass objects appear to be gold for the duration; the source treats 4,000 gp of coins as one cubic foot.
conditions: A viewer can recognize the deception by rolling at or below Intelligence after adding the caster's level to the roll.
A hard strike with cold-wrought iron can dispel the deception: 30%, 25%, 10% or 1%, respectively, for the four component choices.

spells.name: Forget
effect: Erase memory of the previous round, plus another minute for every three caster levels.
conditions: Choose one to four targets: one saves at −2, two at −1, and three or four normally.
exceptions: Existing charms, suggestions, geases and quests remain in force even if their originator is forgotten.
Heal or restoration cast specifically for memory recovery, or wish, can restore what was lost.

spells.name: Leomund'S Trap

fields.Material: Iron pyrite touched to the mechanism

effect: Create a convincing but harmless false trap on a lock, hinge, cap or similar mechanism.
conditions: A trap detector is 80% likely to believe it real, minus 4% for each examiner level beyond first.
An attempted remover is 20% likely to believe removal succeeded, plus 4% per remover level.
Only one such illusion can be placed in a 50′ × 50′ area.
exceptions: Ignoring it causes no actual trap effect.

spells.name: Magic Mouth

fields.Duration: Until its trigger is fulfilled or the magic ends
fields.Material: Small piece of honeycomb

effect: Store a spoken message of at most 25 words, delivered over up to one turn when its specified trigger occurs.
conditions: Use a language known to the caster; the mouth cannot cast spells.
The trigger can be detailed, within a detection distance of ½″ per caster level, as illustrated by the sixth-level/3″ example.
exceptions: The mouth cannot detect invisible creatures, alignment, level or hit dice, or identify class beyond outward dress.
Intelligent animal or plant creatures cannot serve as the enchanted object.

spells.name: Mirror Image
effect: Create 1–4 duplicates that follow the caster's actions, with the count determined by a caster-level-adjusted percentile roll.
A weapon hit destroys an image, including a hit by a magical weapon.
conditions: The images shift between rounds; hitting the real caster once does not identify the caster next round.
exceptions: The printed image-count bands overlap at 75: both 51–75 and 75 or more include that result. The outcome at 75 remains unresolved.

spells.name: Pyrotechnics
effect: Turn a fire into dazzling fireworks that temporarily blind exposed viewers, or a choking smoke cloud that blocks sight beyond two feet.
conditions: Requires a fire within range and extinguishes that source immediately.
Fireworks also affect unobstructed viewers within 12″ of the display; the smoke conforms to a confined space.

spells.name: Ray Of Enfeeblement
effect: Reduce strength-dependent attacks and their physical damage by 25%, plus 2% for each caster level beyond third.
conditions: The reduction applies to physical attacks including missiles, weapons and natural attacks.
exceptions: The DM determines other appropriate consequences of the lost strength.

spells.name: Rope Trick

fields.Area: A 5′–30′ rope and its extradimensional refuge
fields.Material: Powdered corn extract and twisted parchment loop

effect: Suspend a rope whose upper end opens into a concealed extradimensional refuge for the caster and up to five others.
conditions: Only one creature climbs the rope at a time.
With six people inside, the rope cannot also be pulled in; with fewer, it can.
Leave before the spell expires or fall from the original climb height.
exceptions: Climbing only partway can reach an ordinary elevated location without entering the refuge.

spells.name: Scare

fields.Area: One creature below 6 HD or levels
fields.Material: Bone from an undead skeleton, zombie, ghoul, ghast or mummy

effect: Cause trembling fear. A cornered target can fight, but takes −1 to hit, damage and saving throws.
conditions: An encumbered frightened target may drop held items; an unencumbered one does not.
exceptions: Elves, half-elves, the listed undead, larvae, lemures, manes and clerics are unaffected.

spells.name: Shatter

fields.Area: One object up to 100 gp weight/level
fields.Material: Chip of mica

effect: Break a nonmagical crystal, glass, ceramic or porcelain object into fragments.
conditions: The object must fit the spell's weight limit and fail its item saving throw.
exceptions: Magical items and heavier objects are unaffected.

spells.name: Stinking Cloud

fields.Material: Rotten egg or several skunk-cabbage leaves

effect: Create nauseating vapor that makes a creature failing its poison save helpless for 2–5 rounds.
conditions: Even a successful save leaves the creature helpless while in the cloud and for the round after emerging.

spells.name: Strength

fields.Material: Hair or dung from a particularly strong animal

effect: Increase Strength by a class-based roll: cleric or thief 1d6, fighter 1d8, magic-user or monk 1d4.
conditions: Racial, sex and class limits still apply.
For fighters, including paladins and rangers, additions beyond Strength 18 become 10% exceptional-strength increments per point.
exceptions: A fighter already at Strength 18 adds 10%–80% to the exceptional-strength rating.

spells.name: Wizard Lock

fields.Area: Door, chest or portal, up to 30 square feet/level

effect: Magically lock a door, chest or portal.
conditions: It can be defeated by breaking the object, dispel magic, knock, or a magic-user at least four levels above its caster.
exceptions: Knock and the higher-level magic-user's bypass suppress rather than remove the lock.
Extradimensional creatures do not automatically shatter this lock as they do hold portal.

spells.name: Blink
effect: Once each round, vanish and reappear two feet away in a randomly chosen direction; the blink segment is rolled with 2d4.
After that segment, ordinary attacks cannot catch the caster unless they can cover both old and new positions.
conditions: If the destination is occupied, displacement can extend up to ten more feet away from the starting point; a still-blocked destination traps the caster on the Ethereal Plane.
Actions other than a physical attack with a hand-held striking or stabbing weapon have only a 75% chance of functioning correctly.
exceptions: Broad attacks such as breath weapons and fireball can still catch the caster.
The DM determines the result of a failed non-weapon action.

spells.name: Explosive Runes

fields.Saving throw: Reader: none; nearby creatures: half damage

effect: Place dangerous runes on a written document. Reading them detonates them for 6d4+6 damage to the reader and the same damage to nearby creatures, halved on a successful save.
conditions: A magic-user reader has a 5% detection chance per magic-use level; a thief has only 5%.
The caster and instructed magic-users can read safely; the caster can remove the runes at will.
exceptions: Other removal requires dispel magic, not erase.
The explosion destroys the document unless its material normally resists magical fire.

spells.name: Feign Death
effect: Put a willing creature into an apparently dead state: it can hear, smell and remain aware, but cannot see or feel.
Damage is halved; paralysis, poison and energy drain do not affect it while the spell lasts.
conditions: The target's levels or HD cannot exceed the caster's level.
The caster can end the spell, but normal bodily function takes one full round to resume.
exceptions: Poison introduced during the state takes effect when it ends, with a saving throw then allowed.

spells.name: Flame Arrow

fields.Area: One arrow or bolt touched per segment
fields.Material: Drop of oil and small piece of flint

effect: Turn touched arrows or crossbow bolts into magical, burning missiles without a to-hit bonus.
conditions: Each missile must be fired within one round or it burns away.
For the spell's duration the caster can touch one missile each segment.
exceptions: The missile has ordinary ignition chances; a creature especially vulnerable to fire takes one extra point when hit.
This spell does not give every missile extra dice of fire damage.

spells.name: Gust Of Wind

fields.Material: Legume seed

effect: Send a strong gust forward, extinguishing candles, torches and other exposed flames, and toppling light objects.
Lantern-like protected flames have a 5% chance per caster level of going out; large fires flare 1–6 feet downwind.
conditions: Small flying creatures are driven back 1–6″; man-sized flyers cannot advance into the gust; large flyers are slowed by half for one round.

spells.name: Hold Person
effect: Immobilize one to four eligible persons.
conditions: Three or four targets save normally; two save at −1; one saves at −3.

Eligible targets are brownies, dryads, dwarves, elves, gnolls, gnomes, goblins, half-elves, halflings, half-orcs, hobgoblins, humans, kobolds, lizard men, nixies, orcs, pixies, sprites and troglodytes.
exceptions: Partial spell-turning negation can reduce the effect to slow unless the target also saves.

spells.name: Lnfravision

fields.Material: Pinch of dried carrot or an agate

effect: Let the recipient see differences in infrared radiation out to 6″.
conditions: Fire, lanterns and torches interfere with this heat-based sight.
exceptions: Invisibility normally hides a creature from infravision too.

spells.name: Invisibility, 10' Radius

fields.Material: Eyelash enclosed in gum arabic, inherited from invisibility

effect: Apply invisibility to creatures within the spell's area, using the ordinary invisibility rules.
conditions: Affected creatures cannot see one another.
Ordinary noises and other physical clues remain detectable.
exceptions: An affected creature attacking becomes visible by itself, without revealing everyone else.
If the central spell recipient breaks the spell, the shared protection ends.

spells.name: Leomund’S Tiny Hut

fields.Material: Small crystal bead; shatters when the spell ends

effect: Create an outside-opaque shelter, transparent from within, for the caster and up to six other man-sized creatures.
Keep the interior at 70°F while outside temperatures remain from 0°F through 105°F; beyond those limits the inside shifts degree for degree.
conditions: Guests may enter or leave; the caster leaving dissipates the hut.
Wind above 50 mph destroys it; the caster may dimly light or darken the interior.
exceptions: The hut provides no protection against weapons, missiles or spells.

spells.name: Monster Summoning I

fields.Material: Tiny bag and small candle, not necessarily lit

effect: After a 1–4-round delay, summon 2–8 first-level monsters selected by the referee.
They attack the caster's opponents until ordered to stop, slain or the duration expires.
conditions: With no opponent to fight, they can perform other physically possible services if communication is available.
exceptions: The referee determines monster identities and may choose their number to fit the selected monsters' strength.

spells.name: Phantasmal Force

fields.Material: Bit of fleece

effect: Create a visible illusion within the area; believers can suffer its apparent harmful effects.
conditions: Concentrate to maintain it; moving or taking a damaging attack ends concentration.
An opponent striking the illusion ends it unless the caster makes it react appropriately.
A disbeliever may save; successful recognition grants allies +4 on their saves if the discovery is effectively communicated.
exceptions: The illusion has no sound.
Creatures not viewing it are unaffected until they do; the area can move within spell range.

spells.name: Protection from Evil, 10′ Radius

fields.Material: Powdered iron and silver, inherited from the magic-user's first-level version

effect: Extend protection from evil to a ten-foot-radius sphere: evil attacks take −2 to hit protected creatures, and their attack-caused saves gain +2.
The inherited ward prevents bodily contact by the enchanted, conjured or summoned creatures specified by the source.
exceptions: Reverse: protection from good changes the alignment-based protection while retaining the stated exclusion of enchanted evil creatures.

spells.name: Protection From Normal Missiles

fields.Material: Piece of turtle or tortoise shell

effect: Grant immunity to ordinary hurled or projected missiles, including arrows, axes, bolts, javelins, small stones and spears.
Reduce damage from large or magical missiles by one point per damage die.
exceptions: Fireball, lightning bolt and magic missile are magical attacks rather than protected missile forms.

spells.name: Slow

fields.Material: Drop of treacle

effect: Halve affected creatures' current movement and attack rates.
conditions: Choose an area within range containing no more targets than the caster's level.
exceptions: Slow counters haste and can compound an existing slow effect.
The printed magic-user header lists no saving throw.

spells.name: Water Breathing

fields.Material: Short reed or piece of straw

effect: Allow the recipient to breathe freely underwater.
exceptions: Reverse: air breathing allows a water-breathing creature to survive in air.
The magic-user duration is three turns per level, overriding the druid version's longer duration.

spells.name: Charm Monster
effect: Make a living creature regard the caster as a friendly ally and, if communication permits, follow reasonable requests.
Affect 2–8 first-level creatures, 1–4 second-level creatures, 1–2 third-level creatures, or one creature of fourth level or higher.
conditions: Overt hostility by the caster breaks the charm or at least permits a new save, as described by the source.
exceptions: Weekly chance to break charm by monster level or HD: 1st/up to 2: 5%; 2nd/up to 3+2: 10%; 3rd/up to 4+4: 15%; 4th/up to 6: 25%; 5th/up to 7+2: 35%; 6th/up to 8+4: 45%; 7th/up to 10: 60%; 8th/up to 12: 75%; 9th/over 12: 90%.

spells.name: Confusion

fields.Saving throw: Each round at −2; special wandering result
fields.Material: Three nutshells

effect: Confuse a base 2–16 creatures, adding a positive difference between caster level and the strongest opponent's level or HD; affect those nearest the caster.
On a failed save, roll percentile: 01–10 wander away for a turn; 11–60 stand confused; 61–80 attack the nearest creature; 81–00 attack the caster or party.
conditions: Check saves and actions at the beginning of each round.
A creature wandering for a full turn does not make the intervening round-by-round saves.

spells.name: Dig

fields.Material: Miniature shovel and tiny bucket, held throughout excavation

effect: Excavate 125 cubic feet of earth, sand or mud each round, scattering the removed material around the pit.
conditions: Each additional five feet of depth beyond the first five gives a collapse chance of 15% in earth, 35% in sand or 55% in mud.
A creature within one foot of the edge avoids falling with a roll at or below Dexterity; one moving rapidly toward it saves versus magic.
A creature in the newly excavated center falls automatically.
exceptions: This spell excavates the listed loose materials; it does not state that it cuts solid rock.

spells.name: Enchanted Weapon

fields.Area: Two small weapons or one large weapon
fields.Material: Powdered lime and carbon

effect: Make an ordinary weapon count as a +1 magical weapon for its ability to affect protected targets, without granting attack or damage bonuses.
conditions: A successful hit with an enchanted missile weapon ends that enchantment; other affected weapons last for the duration.
exceptions: Gap: the header marks the spell reversible, but this paragraph does not explain the reverse's operation.

spells.name: Extension I
effect: Increase the duration of a previously cast first-, second- or third-level spell by 50%.
conditions: The spell being extended must have a meaningful duration.
exceptions: Range, area and other effects are not increased by this description.

spells.name: Fear

fields.Material: Hen's heart or white feather
fields.Area: 6″ long cone, 3″ diameter at end and ½′ at base

effect: Panic affected creatures into fleeing at their fastest speed, beginning on the round after casting.
Held items may be dropped immediately: 60% at one HD or level, reduced by 5% for each additional HD or level, reaching 0% at thirteenth.
conditions: The cone reaches 6″ and is 3″ across at its far end.

spells.name: Fire Charm

fields.Area: 30′-diameter fire source and its surrounding veil
fields.Material: Exceptionally thin multicolored silk thrown into the fire

effect: Surround a normal fire with dancing colored flame; observers failing their saves stand motionless, transfixed.
conditions: The charmed creature may be targeted by a separate suggestion spell of twelve or fewer words, saving at −3.
Physical attack or a solid obstruction blocking the viewer's sight of the flames breaks the charm.
exceptions: Passing through the veil burns like the original ordinary fire; it is not itself magical fire.

spells.name: Fire Trap

fields.Material: Sulfur or saltpeter traced around the closure

effect: Trap a closable object so unauthorized entry or touching detonates it for 1d4 + 1 HP per caster level; a successful save halves damage.
conditions: The caster can use the object safely, and the explosion does not harm the trapped object.
Detection is only half as likely as normal; a failed removal attempt triggers it.

With hold portal, only the first spell works, or neither if simultaneous. If wizard lock already exists, fire trap fails; simultaneous casting negates both, while adding wizard lock later has a 50% chance to negate both.
exceptions: Knock does not neutralize a fire trap.

spells.name: Fumble

fields.Saving throw: Special; successful save gives slow-like effect
fields.Material: Dab of solidified milkfat

effect: Make the target stumble when running and drop items or weapons when trying to handle them.
conditions: Recovering from a fall or retrieving a dropped object usually consumes the next full round.
Dropped breakable objects may be damaged.
exceptions: Even a successful save reduces the victim to half normal efficiency, as with slow.

spells.name: Hallucinatory Terrain

fields.Duration: Until dispelled or contacted by an intelligent creature
fields.Material: Stone, twig and green leaf or grass

effect: Disguise real terrain as a different natural feature, such as making a road look like a marsh or a precipice like a gentle slope.
conditions: The illusion ends when an intelligent creature contacts it or dispel magic affects the area.
exceptions: The printed area header gives 1″ × 1″ square per level, while its 10th- and 12th-level examples give 10″ × 10″ and 12″ × 12″ squares. Their scaling is inconsistent; the intended area remains unresolved.

spells.name: Ice Storm

fields.Material: Pinch of dust and a few drops of water

effect: Choose hail that deals 3d10 damage to creatures in its area, or sleet that blinds creatures for the duration.
Sleet makes the ground icy, halves movement and gives moving creatures a 50% chance to slip and fall.
exceptions: It negates heat metal, but the first hail application still causes damage while doing so.

spells.name: Massmorph

fields.Duration: Until the caster ends it or dispel magic is cast
fields.Material: Handful of bark chips

effect: Make up to ten willing man-sized or smaller creatures per caster level appear to be ordinary trees.
conditions: Recipients must be within the spell's area.
exceptions: Others may pass among and touch the apparent trees without exposing the illusion.
Blows reveal their living nature through wounds and blood.
The printed area header appears to read 11′ × 1″ square per level. This unusual dimensional expression remains unresolved.

spells.name: Minor Globe of Invulnerability

fields.Material: Glass or crystal bead

effect: Prevent first-, second- and third-level spell effects from entering the sphere.
exceptions: Spells cast outward from within work normally.
Fourth-level and higher spells penetrate; dispel magic can bring down the globe.

spells.name: Monster Summoning II

fields.Material: Tiny bag and small candle, as monster summoning I

effect: After a 1–4-round delay, summon 1–6 second-level monsters.
Use the first summoning spell's instructions: fight the caster's opponents until stopped, slain or the duration ends.
conditions: Other services require communication and physical capability.
exceptions: The referee selects the actual monsters.

spells.name: Plant Growth
effect: Thicken existing vegetation into a tangled barrier, reducing passage to 1″ movement or 2″ for larger-than-man-sized creatures.
conditions: The area must already contain brush or trees.
The overgrowth persists until cleared by work, fire or suitable magic.
exceptions: Gap: the inherited druid examples scale square dimensions differently from a literal reading of the area header; verify the intended area with the DM/source.

spells.name: Polymorph Other

fields.Material: Caterpillar cocoon

effect: Transform a creature's form and capabilities; surviving the change requires a system-shock roll.
The daily chance to assume the new personality is 100% − 5% × original Intelligence + 5% × (new HD − original HD or character level).
Until personality changes, the recipient can retain its prior knowledge while using the new body's capabilities.
conditions: The spell cannot turn a lower-Intelligence creature into a higher-Intelligence one.
Use dispel magic to restore the original form, with another system-shock check.
exceptions: The original creature's toughness is not erased merely by assuming a tiny or harmless-looking shape.

spells.name: Polymorph Self
effect: Assume forms from a wren's size through a hippopotamus's size, gaining their means of locomotion.
Change forms repeatedly if desired, spending five segments each time; returning to the original form restores 1d12 HP.
conditions: The chosen form must have enough strength for its normal movement.
exceptions: No system-shock or personality-change check is required.
The spell grants no new attack powers, magical abilities, special senses or defensive powers; damage remains damage to the caster.

spells.name: Rary'S Mnemonic Enhancer

fields.Material: String, ivory plaque worth at least 100 gp, and ink of squid secretion plus black-dragon blood or giant-slug digestive juice

effect: Memorize or retain three additional spell levels: three first-level spells, one first plus one second, or one third-level spell.
conditions: Choose additional immediate memorization or retention of a spell cast with the enhancer's aid.
exceptions: All listed material components disappear on casting.

spells.name: Remove Curse

fields.Saving throw: Special; reverse is negated by a successful save

effect: Remove a curse or similar unwanted influence; a cursed weapon, shield or armor usually stays cursed, but its bearer can typically discard it.

Reverse: bestow curse lasts one turn per caster level. Its listed random outcomes are a random ability reduced to 3 (50%), −4 to hit and saves (25%), or a 50% chance each turn to drop held items or do nothing (25%).
conditions: The reverse requires touching the victim, who still receives a saving throw.
exceptions: A DM-approved alternative curse should have comparable power.

spells.name: Wall Of Fire

fields.Area: Sheet up to 2″ square/level, or ring of radius 1″ + ¼″/level and height 2″
fields.Material: Phosphorus

effect: Passing through deals 2d6 + 1 HP per caster level; the hot side deals 2d4 within 1″ and 1d4 within 2″.
Only the side away from the caster inflicts damage; undead take double normal damage.
conditions: The sheet is stationary; the ring moves with the caster.
exceptions: Creatures specially vulnerable to fire may take additional damage.

spells.name: Wall Of Ice

fields.Area: One inch thick and 1″ square area per caster level
fields.Material: Small quartz or similar rock crystal

effect: Create a defensive sheet of ice. Breaking through deals 2 HP per inch of thickness, or 3 to fire-using creatures and 1 to cold-using creatures.
conditions: A horizontal sheet dropped on opponents acts like ice storm's hail.
A fireball or fiery dragon breath melts the wall in one round, producing steam fog lasting one turn.
exceptions: Normal fires and lesser magical fires do not speed its melting.

spells.name: Wizard Eye

fields.Material: Bit of bat fur

effect: Create an invisible eye that transmits visual information to the caster.
It travels 3″ per round looking ahead, or 1″ per round while inspecting ceiling, walls and floor.
conditions: It can move in any direction for the duration.
Its infravision reaches 10 feet; in bright light it sees up to 60 feet.

spells.name: Fire Shield

fields.Material: Hot version: phosphorus; cold version: live firefly/glowworm or tails of four dead ones

effect: Surround the caster with dim flames. An attacker hitting with its body or a hand-held weapon deals normal damage but suffers twice that damage in return.
Choose hot flames for +2 on saves against cold and half damage on failure or none on success; choose cold flames for the equivalent protection against fire.
conditions: The flames shed only dim light within 15 feet.
exceptions: The opposite element remains dangerous: with hot flames, a failed fire save doubles damage; with cold flames, a failed cold save doubles damage.

spells.name: Airy Water

fields.Material: Handful of alkaline or bromine salts

effect: Turn water or a water-based liquid into a less dense, breathable medium within a globe that moves with the caster.
conditions: Air-breathing companions in the area can move and breathe as in air.
exceptions: Water-breathing creatures cannot breathe in it; intelligent ones can enter only if they can move without swimming.

spells.name: Animal Growth

fields.Components: V, S; material also specified in text
fields.Area: Up to eight animals in a 2″ square
fields.Material: Pinch of powdered bone

effect: Double affected animals' size, HD and combat damage, with the associated improvement in attacks.
exceptions: Reverse: halve size, HD and attack damage.
The magic-user duration is one round per level, overriding the inherited druid duration.
Gap: the header omits M although the paragraph explicitly requires powdered bone.

spells.name: Animate Dead

fields.Area: Up to one skeleton or zombie/level
fields.Material: Drop of blood, piece of human flesh, and bone powder or a bone shard

effect: Animate dead human bones or bodies as skeletons or zombies that obey commands, such as guarding an area.
conditions: Animation persists until the undead are destroyed or the magic is dispelled.
exceptions: The source cautions that animating dead is not intrinsically a good act.

spells.name: Bigby'S Interposing Hand

fields.Area: Hand placed between caster and chosen opponent
fields.Material: Glove

effect: Create a hand that stays between the caster and one opponent, changing position as the opponent tries to get around it.
conditions: Choose a hand size from human to titan-sized.
It takes as many HP of damage to destroy as the caster has.
exceptions: A creature weighing less than 2,000 pounds trying to push past it is reduced to half movement.

spells.name: Cloudkill
effect: Kill creatures below 4+1 HD outright. Those from 4+1 through 5+1 HD save versus poison at −4; stronger creatures through 6 HD save normally or die.
conditions: The cloud rolls away from the caster at 1″ per round, following low ground and descending openings.
Wind can redirect it, but not back toward its caster.
exceptions: Strong wind disperses it in four rounds; greater wind prevents casting.
Very thick vegetation disperses it after two rounds of passage.

spells.name: Conjure Elemental

fields.Material: Air: burning incense; earth: soft clay; fire: sulfur and phosphorus; water: water and sand

effect: Conjure an air, earth, fire or water elemental, choosing the type when memorizing the spell.
conditions: Fire and water versions also require a substantial source of the appropriate element within range.
Concentrate to control it within 3″ per caster level; wounds or grappling break concentration.
Even with concentration, there is a 5% chance of rebellion at the end of the second round and each later round.
exceptions: An uncontrolled elemental seeks to attack the conjurer, though it does not abandon an ongoing combat to do so.
A water elemental is destroyed if it moves more than 6″ from a body of water.
The source points to protective circles, pentacles and protection from evil as safeguards.

spells.name: Cone Of Cold

fields.Area: Cone from caster’s hand, ½″ long per level
fields.Material: Tiny crystal or glass cone

effect: Drain heat for (1d4+1) damage per caster level; the printed tenth-level example deals 10d4+10.

spells.name: Contact Other Plane
effect: Contact a randomly reached, often resentful extraplanar power for brief answers such as yes, no, maybe or unknown.
Ask one question per two caster levels; more distant contacts tend to know more but create greater danger.
A reply is not guaranteed to be knowledgeable or truthful.
conditions: Each Intelligence point above 15 reduces the insanity probability by 5%.
Insanity begins as soon as the first question is asked and can last one week per plane removed, to ten weeks.
The source gives a 1% death risk per plane before recovery unless remove curse is used.
exceptions: Plane: insanity / knowledge / truthfulness: elemental 20% / 90% / 75%; 1 removed 5% / 60% / 65%; 2 removed 10% / 65% / 67%; 3 removed 15% / 70% / 70%; 4 removed 20% / 75% / 73%; 5 removed 25% / 80% / 75%; 6 removed 30% / 85% / 78%; 7 removed 35% / 90% / 81%; 8 removed 40% / 95% / 85%; 9 or more removed 50% / 98% / 90%. Elemental knowledge assumes a question about the appropriate elemental plane.

spells.name: Distance Distortion

fields.Material: Small lump of soft clay

effect: Use an earth elemental to make the affected route effectively half as long and wide, or twice as long and wide, for travelers.
conditions: The caster must already have conjured an earth elemental; it cooperates when told that distance distortion is intended.
The elemental returns to its plane when the duration ends.
exceptions: Travelers cannot detect the true dimensions by ordinary means; a faint magical aura remains, and true seeing reveals the spread-out elemental.

spells.name: Extension II
effect: Increase a previously cast first- through fourth-level spell's duration by 50%.
conditions: The underlying duration must be meaningful.
exceptions: This expands the eligible spell levels of extension I; it does not increase the percentage.

spells.name: Feeblemind

fields.Saving throw: Negates; spell-user category adjusts the roll
fields.Material: Handful of small clay, crystal, glass or mineral spheres

effect: Severely impair the mental faculties of a person or creature that uses spells.
conditions: The inherited save adjustments are cleric +1, druid −1, human magic-user −4, illusionist −5, and combination or nonhuman spell-user −2.
exceptions: Heal, restoration or wish can remove the effect.

spells.name: Hold Monster

fields.Material: One small hard-metal rod or bar per target

effect: Immobilize one to four creatures of any type that the caster can see.
conditions: Three or four targets save normally, two at −1, and one at −3.
exceptions: Partial negation reduces the effect to slow.

spells.name: Leomund's Secret Chest

fields.Material: Masterwork chest costing at least 5,000 gp and a perfect miniature of the same materials

effect: Send a chest to the Ethereal Plane, recalling it while holding its miniature. It stores one cubic foot per caster level despite its apparent dimensions.
conditions: The caster can have only one chest/replica pair, even with wish.
Touch the chest and hold its replica when casting; living contents give a 75% chance of spell failure.
After day 60 the unretrieved chest has a cumulative 5% daily chance of permanent loss.
exceptions: Losing or destroying the miniature prevents recovery, even by wish.
The chest has a cumulative 1% weekly chance of ethereal interference; retrieval opens a five-hour window with an initial 5% chance of an ethereal creature crossing, decreasing by 1% each hour.
If the chest is found on the Ethereal Plane: 10% it is ignored, 10% something is added, 30% contents exchanged, 30% something stolen, and 20% emptied.

spells.name: Magic Jar

fields.Material: Large gem or crystal as life-force receptacle

effect: Place the caster's life force in a gem or crystal, then attempt to possess a creature within range; each attempt takes one round.
A humanoid host allows the caster's own spell use; only rudimentary host knowledge is available, not its languages or spells.
conditions: The jar must initially be within range of the caster's body. It senses nearby creatures without identifying what they are.
Compare caster and victim mental ability scores using the printed modifier table. The source combines Intelligence and Wisdom, with an Intelligence-only exception for nonhuman/nonhumanoid creatures.

A host retries its save each round for a difference below 5, each turn at 5–8, each day at 9–12 and each week at 13+. Regaining control traps the possessor until control is recovered or escape is possible.
Returning to the original body takes one round and requires the jar to be in range.
exceptions: A failed possession leaves the caster in the jar.
Destroying the original body does not itself harm the life force in the jar; destroying the jar extinguishes that life force.
Caster-minus-victim mental-score difference and victim save adjustment: −9 or less +4; −8 to −6 +3; −5 to −3 +2; −2 to 0 +1; +1 to +4 0; +5 to +8 −1; +9 to +12 −2; +13 or more −3.

spells.name: Monster Summoning III

fields.Material: Tiny bag and small candle, inherited from monster summoning I

effect: After a 1–4-round delay, summon 1–4 third-level monsters using the lesser summoning spell's command rules.
conditions: They fight the caster's opponents until stopped, slain or the duration ends; other services require communication and physical capability.
exceptions: The referee selects the monsters.

spells.name: Mordenkainen's Faithful Hound

fields.Material: Tiny silver whistle, bone fragment and thread

effect: Create a watchdog visible only to its caster that barks when a creature larger than a cat approaches its guarded location.
If an intruder exposes its back, the hound attacks as a 10-HD monster for 3d6 damage, able to hit even creatures requiring +3 or better weapons.
conditions: The hound detects invisible, astral, ethereal, out-of-phase and similar hidden creatures.
The caster moving more than 3″ from the guarded area automatically ends the spell.
exceptions: The hound cannot be attacked, but can be dispelled.

spells.name: Passwall

fields.Material: Pinch of sesame seeds

effect: Open a temporary passage through a wooden, plaster or stone wall.
conditions: Several castings can connect into a deeper passage through a thick wall.

spells.name: Stone Shape

fields.Material: Soft clay shaped roughly as desired, then touched to the stone

effect: Reshape existing stone into a useful object or opening, such as a weapon, coffer or escape route.
conditions: The entire affected stone volume must fit the limit.
exceptions: The spell does not produce fine detail.

spells.name: Telekinesis

fields.Area: Object or creature up to 250 gp weight/level

effect: Move a target vertically or horizontally by concentration: 2″ in the first round, then 4″, 8″, 16″ and onward, doubling to a maximum 1,024″ per round.
conditions: A target that grows beyond the weight limit escapes the effect.
Before speed reaches 16″ per round, walking or other motive power can counter it.
exceptions: Bigby's hand spells and other appropriate magic can counter the movement.
High-speed objects can be dangerous, but this paragraph gives no universal collision-damage formula.

spells.name: Transmute Rock To Mud

fields.Material: Clay and water; reverse uses sand, lime and water

effect: Turn natural rock into an equal volume of mud. Creatures unable to escape can sink and suffocate, except those light enough to cross such ground.
conditions: Mud depth cannot exceed half its length or breadth.
Drying into ordinary dirt takes 1–6 days per cubic inch on the spell scale, depending on conditions.
exceptions: Reverse: mud to rock permanently hardens ordinary mud into soft stone.
Dispel magic or the reverse restores substance, but not necessarily the original shape.

spells.name: Wall Of Force

fields.Area: Up to 20 square feet/level, including sphere or hemisphere
fields.Material: Pinch of powdered diamond

effect: Create a stationary invisible barrier that blocks weapons, missiles, heat, cold, electricity, spells and breath weapons in either direction.
exceptions: Dispel magic does not remove it; disintegrate destroys it.
It cannot be moved once placed.

spells.name: Wall Of Iron

fields.Material: Small piece of sheet iron

effect: Create a vertical iron wall that can merge into surrounding material to seal an opening.
conditions: Without support the wall falls and crushes creatures beneath it.
exceptions: It can be dispelled and remains subject to normal iron hazards such as rust and physical damage.

spells.name: Wall Of Stone

fields.Material: Small granite block

effect: Create a granite wall joined to existing rock. It can form a barrier, bridge or ramp rather than only a vertical wall.
conditions: It must merge with an existing stone formation, but does not need a separate firm foundation.
exceptions: Dispel magic, disintegrate or ordinary destruction can remove it.

spells.name: Anti-Magic Shell
effect: Surround the caster with a moving barrier that excludes magic and magical effects, including the listed breath, gaze and voice attacks.
Magic items and spells do not function inside the shell; charmed, summoned and conjured creatures cannot enter.
exceptions: Ordinary creatures, physical missiles and mundane weapons can pass through.
A magic sword loses its magical function inside, but remains a physical sword.

spells.name: Bigby’S Forceful Hand

fields.Material: Glove

effect: Interpose a magical hand as with Bigby's interposing hand, adding force that pushes creatures of 500 pounds or less away.
The source slows creatures in the 500–2,000-pound band to 1″ per round, and creatures up to 8,000 pounds to half speed.
conditions: The hand has as many HP as its caster.

spells.name: Control Weather

fields.Material: Burning incense and earth/wood fragments mixed in water

effect: Change sky or precipitation, temperature and wind within the transitions allowed by the current conditions.
conditions: The weather begins changing after an additional 1–4 turns.
Changes must remain climatically plausible; incompatible combinations such as fog with strong wind are excluded.
Multiple castings work only successively, not simultaneously.
exceptions: Permitted changes from prevailing cloud/precipitation: clear to very clear or light clouds/haze; partly cloudy to clear, cloudy, mist/light rain/small hail, or sleet/light snow; cloudy to partly cloudy, deep clouds, fog, heavy rain/large hail, or driving sleet/heavy snow.

Temperature: hot to warm or sweltering; warm to hot or cool; cool to warm or cold; cold to cool or arctic. Wind: calm to dead calm or light breeze; light wind to calm or strong; strong to light or gale; gale to strong or storm; storm to gale, hurricane or typhoon.

spells.name: Death Spell

fields.Material: Crushed black pearl worth at least 1,000 gp

effect: Slay creatures instantly, with the number depending on HD: below 2 HD, 4d20; 2–4 HD, 3d10; 4+1–6+3 HD, 2d4; 6+4–8+3 HD, 1d4.
conditions: Mixed-HD groups use the printed conversion procedure rather than independently applying every row.
exceptions: Lycanthropes, undead and creatures from outside the Prime Material Plane are unaffected.

Mixed-HD conversion: one 2–4 HD creature equals four below-2 HD; one 4+1–6+3 HD creature equals eight below-2 HD or three 2–4 HD; one 6+4–8+3 HD creature equals ten below-2 HD, five 2–4 HD, or two 4+1–6+3 HD. Roll below-2 HD total and expend equivalents; insufficient remainder leaves the higher-HD creature alive. The source also permits applying higher-HD creatures first.

spells.name: Disintegrate

fields.Saving throw: Negates for a creature or saving-throw-capable magical target
fields.Area: One creature or one object up to 1 cubic ″
fields.Material: Lodestone and pinch of dust

effect: Make matter vanish, including a single living or undead creature, or qualifying ordinary or magical material.
exceptions: It can destroy magical matter or energy such as a Bigby's forceful hand, but not a globe of invulnerability or anti-magic shell.

spells.name: Enchant An Item

fields.Casting time: 16 hours + 8–64 hours, working at most 8 hours/day
fields.Saving throw: Item uses caster's save versus magic; bonuses capped at +3
fields.Material: Varies with the item and intended magic; DM determines the required substances

effect: Prepare a high-quality, undamaged item to receive magical enchantments. Materials and craftsmanship must be the finest suitable; raw materials normally exceed 100 gp.
The final preparation save uses the caster's score, with no more than +3 in bonuses; a natural 1 fails.
conditions: Maintain touch while working and keep the item within one foot during rest. Work cannot be accelerated, and rest permits no other magic or active work.
Start the first added spell within 24 hours of preparation, and each later spell within 24 hours of the previous one, even after a failure.
Each added spell requires four hours plus another 4–8 hours per spell level, with touch/proximity maintained as above.
exceptions: Each added spell requires its own save; only the initial preparation's success is immediately known.
Permanency is needed for lasting magic and risks Constitution loss; charged items cannot be made permanent.
Scrolls and magic devices cannot supply the preparation or the added spellcasting.

spells.name: Extension III
effect: Double the duration of a previously cast first-, second- or third-level spell.
Extend fourth- or fifth-level spells by 50% instead.
conditions: The spell must have a meaningful duration.

spells.name: Geas
effect: Impose a service or prohibition that the target must follow; outright refusal brings sickness and death within 1–4 weeks.
Deviating from or twisting the instructions causes a corresponding Strength loss until the deviation ends.
conditions: The target must be conscious and acting under its own volition.
The command cannot demand suicide or acts likely to mean certain death.
exceptions: Wish can remove it; dispel magic and remove curse cannot.
An improperly framed geas can be void immediately; the DM adjudicates its wording and fulfillment.

spells.name: Glassee

fields.Material: Small glass or crystal piece

effect: See through up to four inches of metal, six feet of stone or twenty feet of wood.
conditions: Choose a view only the caster can use, applying it up to once per round, or make an actual one-way transparent section.
exceptions: Lead, gold and platinum are unaffected.
Transparency does not create a physical opening.

spells.name: Globe Of Invulnerability

fields.Material: Glass or crystal bead, inherited from minor globe

effect: Exclude first- through fourth-level spell effects from the protected sphere.
exceptions: The caster can cast spells outward through it.
Higher-level spells still function; the inherited minor-globe rules allow dispel magic to remove the globe.

spells.name: Guards And Wards

fields.Material: Burning incense, sulfur and oil, knotted string, umber-hulk blood and small silver rod
fields.Area: 1″ radius/level extending from a 2″ diameter sphere

effect: Ward a stronghold with ten-foot visibility in misty corridors, wizard-locked doors, webbed stairs and pervasive magical detection.
Hide one door per caster level as a wall, and give intruders at directional choices a 50% chance to believe they are going the opposite way.
conditions: With full familiarity, also choose one extra: dancing lights in four corridors, magic mouths in two locations, stinking clouds in two locations, gust of wind in one room/corridor, or suggestion in one place.
The hidden doors and optional extra effect require full familiarity with the area.
exceptions: Dispel magic removes one random effect per casting; remove curse does not work.

spells.name: Invisible Stalker

fields.Material: Burning incense and horn carved into a crescent

effect: Summon an 8-HD invisible stalker bound to carry out assigned tasks, even at very great distances.
conditions: It serves under compulsion, not loyalty.
exceptions: Prolonged or complicated tasks invite resentful interpretations; use the referenced Monster Manual entry for the creature's full behavior and statistics.

spells.name: Legend Lore

fields.Casting time: Present subject: 1–4 turns; detailed knowledge: 1–10 days; rumors only: 2–12 weeks
fields.Material: Incense, ivory strips forming a rectangle, and an additional sacrificed offering

effect: Discover whether significant lore exists, often as a cryptic clue to information or its location.
conditions: The subject must actually be noteworthy or legendary.
Being at the place or having the person/object present improves the result and shortens casting.
During casting, engage only in routine necessities such as eating and sleeping.
exceptions: Results can be riddles, rhymes, ciphers or other indirect clues rather than a plain factual answer.

spells.name: Lower Water

fields.Material: Small vial of water and small vial of dust

effect: Lower water or similar fluid by 5% of its original level per caster level, using the cleric spell's basic procedure.
exceptions: The reverse raises water by ½′ per caster level, using the magic-user version’s reduced rise.

spells.name: Monster Summoning IV

fields.Material: Tiny bag and small candle, inherited from monster summoning I

effect: After a 1–3-round delay, summon 1–3 fourth-level monsters.
conditions: Use the original summoning spell's combat commands and service limits.
exceptions: The referee selects the actual monsters.

spells.name: Move Earth

fields.Casting time: One turn for each 4″ square area
fields.Material: Bag of mixed soils and iron blade

effect: Move dirt, clay, loam or sand to collapse banks or reshape earthen features.
conditions: Moving whole terrain features requires subsequently summoning an earth elemental to assist.
Finish all required spellcasting and summoning before any movement occurs.
exceptions: Rock outcrops cannot be collapsed or moved by this spell.

spells.name: Otiluke's Freezing Sphere

fields.Saving throw: Ray: negates; bursting globe: half damage
fields.Area: Freezing surface, narrow ray or 10′-radius cold burst
fields.Material: Surface: one-inch crystal sheet; ray: white sapphire worth at least 1,000 gp; globe: diamond worth at least 1,000 gp

effect: Choose a surface-freezing form that freezes water six inches deep over 100 square feet per caster level, lasting one round per level.
Alternatively, fire a narrow ray for four HP of damage per caster level; a successful save avoids it, and other things along its remaining path must also save if applicable.
Or create a cool, sling-stone-sized globe that shatters on impact for 4d6 cold damage within ten feet.
conditions: The unthrown globe automatically shatters after one round per caster level, endangering anyone nearby.
exceptions: Every listed material component is consumed.

spells.name: Part Water

fields.Area: Trough: 3′ deep × 1′ wide × 2″ long per level
fields.Material: Two small sheets of crystal or glass

effect: Part water or a similar liquid into a traversable trough sized by caster level.
conditions: The caster may end the effect before the duration expires.
exceptions: Use this magic-user range and duration instead of the cleric version's values.

spells.name: Project Image

fields.Material: Small doll or replica of the caster

effect: Project a duplicate that walks, speaks and performs the caster's chosen actions; the caster's spells actually originate from the image.
conditions: Keep the image in the caster's sight at all times; an obstructed view ends the spell.
exceptions: Physical attacks do not affect it.
The caster can dismiss it, and dispel magic can remove it.

spells.name: Reincarnation

fields.Material: Small drum and drop of blood

effect: Return a dead person in a new body appearing after 1–6 turns, without a system-shock or resurrection-survival check.
conditions: Death must have occurred within one day per caster level.
The person retains most former memories, while the new body can change class, abilities and speech.
Very good or very evil people do not return as a creature of the opposite general alignment.
exceptions: New body, d100: 01–05 bugbear; 06–11 dwarf; 12–18 elf; 19–23 gnoll; 24–28 gnome; 29–33 goblin; 34–40 half-elf; 41–47 halfling; 48–54 half-orc; 55–59 hobgoblin; 60–73 human; 74–79 kobold; 80–85 orc; 86–90 ogre; 91–95 ogre mage; 96–00 troll.
The person recalls most former life and memories, but abilities, class and speech may differ in the new form.

spells.name: Repulsion

fields.Material: Two magnetized iron bars joined to ivory and ebony canine statuettes

effect: Drive creatures in the path away from the caster; the source gives a speed of 3″ per round or the approaching creature's own motive speed.
conditions: A repelled creature completes its movement away even if that carries it beyond spell range.
exceptions: Gap: the source's alternative movement-rate wording needs adjudication; no universal choice between the two rates is added here.

spells.name: Spiritwrack

fields.Casting time: Special; prepared document then sequential reading
fields.Saving throw: Initial magic-resistance check adjusted for caster level
fields.Material: Personally illuminated vellum with the being's name, gold-leaf border, ruby ink and type I–III demon ichor; at least 1,000 gp supplies plus 5,000 gp ruby powder

effect: Read a specially prepared condemnation that roots the named being unless it resists with magic resistance.
The second round inflicts one HP per HD; the third removes half its remaining HP and ends by confining it on its own plane for a number of years equal to caster level.
conditions: Preparing the document takes 8–32 hours; the being must be present itself, not merely possessing another creature.
It cannot attack the reader while the reading continues. If it resists and is not otherwise bound, it is 90% likely to retreat to another plane.
Each round gives a cumulative 25% chance of submission without payment.
exceptions: Completing the punishment makes the being the caster's permanent enemy.

spells.name: Stone to Flesh

fields.Area: One formerly living creature of any size, or 9 cubic feet of ordinary stone/level
fields.Material: Earth and blood; reverse uses lime, water and earth

effect: Restore a petrified creature, including its belongings, to living flesh, subject to a system-shock survival roll.
Ordinary stone can instead become flesh within the volume limit.
exceptions: Reverse: flesh to stone petrifies the creature and its carried possessions; the intended victim receives a saving throw.

spells.name: Tenser's Transformation

fields.Material: Potion of heroism or superheroism consumed during casting

effect: Double the caster's HP, improving AC by four and attacking on the fighter matrix at the caster's level.
Make two dagger attacks per round, each dealing an additional two HP of damage.
conditions: Damage first consumes the additional magical HP; damage beyond that pool costs two real HP per point.
The transformed caster continues attacking until opponents are slain, the caster dies, dispel magic ends it, or duration expires.
exceptions: Only a dagger may be used for these attacks; the caster cannot simply choose to stop the berserk transformation.

spells.name: Bigby'S Grasping Hand

fields.Material: Leather glove

effect: Hold a creature or object weighing up to 1,000 pounds motionless, or push with twice the strength of Bigby's Forceful Hand.
The inherited hand persists between the caster and the chosen opponent and withstands damage equal to its caster's HP.
exceptions: The source calls the hand twice as strong as Forceful Hand. For comparison, the original hand pushes creatures of 500 pounds or less away, slows creatures weighing 500–2,000 pounds to 1″ per round, and slows creatures up to 8,000 pounds by half.

spells.name: Cacodemon

fields.Area: One named type IV, V or VI demon
fields.Material: Five flaming black candles; hot coals burning sulfur, bat hair, lard, soot, mercuric-nitric acid crystals, mandrake, alcohol and named parchment; dish of mammal blood

effect: Call a named type IV, V or VI demon, unusually strong at eight HP per HD.
A roll above caster level on 3d6 makes the summoning fail; use 2d10 for a type VI demon.
conditions: The caster needs a protective circle or protected thaumaturgic triangle, and the demon must be confined in a pentagram.
An interrupted casting fails. Interruption after arrival gives a 10% escape chance, rising cumulatively each further interrupted round.
Service can be coerced with spiritwrack, bargained for, or secured after trap the soul; the demon follows exact pledges rather than their intended spirit.
exceptions: An impossibly long or impossible service has a 50% chance to free it from its obligations; such a freed demon can remain for up to 666 days.

The caster may coerce service with spiritwrack and the demon’s pledge, bargain using fresh human blood and the promise of at least one human sacrifice, or imprison it with trap the soul. A coerced demon resents the caster permanently; bargaining binds the demon to the exact pledge rather than its spirit.

A trapped demon may bargain before imprisonment; once imprisoned it remains until the possessor breaks its container. On release, it performs one service if required, then returns to the Abyss; if no service is demanded it is free to act.

spells.name: Charm Plants

fields.Material: Pinch of humus, drop of water, and twig or leaf

effect: Communicate with affected plants and command them to use their existing abilities.
conditions: Only intelligent plants receive the saving throw.
exceptions: The spell grants no new movement or other capabilities.

spells.name: Delayed Blast Fire Ball

fields.Material: Tiny ball of bat guano and sulfur, inherited from fireball

effect: Create a fireball dealing 1d6+1 damage per caster level; choose its detonation delay when casting.
conditions: The chosen delay ranges from one-tenth of a round to five rounds.
exceptions: The inherited fireball expands through the available space to its full volume, ignites combustibles and can detonate early if its traveling streak hits a material obstruction.

spells.name: Drawmij's Instant Summons

fields.Range: Unlimited on the same plane; planar reach depends on level
fields.Material: Gem worth at least 5,000 gp, crushed to complete the spell

effect: Prepare a summons for one specifically named item previously touched during the initial incantation, then speak the final word and crush the same gem to bring it to a chosen hand.
conditions: The item cannot exceed a sword's length or about 75 gp weight.
If another creature possesses it, the summons fails but identifies its possessor and approximate location.
At level 14 an unpossessed item can be one plane removed; each later level adds one further plane.
exceptions: Possession need not mean physically holding the object.

spells.name: Duo-Dimension

fields.Material: Flat ivory likeness costing about 5,000–10,000 gp and parchment strip; both consumed

effect: Become two-dimensional, turning invisible when edge-on and passing through thin gaps with sufficient height.
The caster can act normally, including alternating visible spellcasting and edge-on movement.
conditions: While edge-on, attacks cannot affect the caster; while visible, attacks deal triple normal damage.
A portion of the caster exists astrally, risking notice from Astral creatures; if noticed, an astral attack has a 25% chance to pull the caster entirely there.

spells.name: Limited Wish

fields.Casting time: Time to speak the request; six seconds per segment

effect: Grant a carefully worded, limited alteration of events or effects, often only partly or temporarily.
conditions: The spell cannot substantially rewrite major realities or supply wealth or experience merely on request.
Possible uses include temporary healing, modifying combat chances or magical duration, favorable disposition, or a minor clue.
exceptions: Literal wording matters; excessive demands can have adverse interpretations.

spells.name: Mass Invisibility

fields.Material: Eyelash enclosed in gum arabic, inherited from invisibility

effect: Apply invisibility on a much larger scale: about 300–400 man-sized creatures, 30–40 giants or 6–8 large dragons in the area.
conditions: The underlying invisibility hides ordinary and infrared sight, not sound or physical evidence.
Affected allies need a means of perceiving invisibility to see invisible companions.
exceptions: Gap: the short mass-spell paragraph does not resolve group-wide ending behavior separately; use the underlying invisibility rules with the DM.

spells.name: Monster Summoning V

fields.Material: Tiny bag and small candle, inherited from monster summoning I

effect: After 1–3 rounds, summon 1–2 fifth-level monsters selected by the referee.
conditions: They attack the caster's opponents until stopped, slain or the duration ends.
Other services require communication and physical capability.
exceptions: The printed casting time is six segments despite this being a seventh-level spell.

spells.name: Mordenkainen'S Sword

fields.Material: Miniature platinum sword with copper-and-zinc fittings costing 500 gp; disappears afterward

effect: Attack as a fighter of half the caster's level, with no magical to-hit bonus but the ability to strike even +3-only, astral, ethereal or out-of-phase opponents.
A roll of 19 or 20 hits any AC. Damage is 5–20 against man-sized or smaller targets and 5–30 against larger ones.
conditions: Directing the sword excludes activities other than movement.
exceptions: It can strike to subdue.
It ends when dismissed, when its duration expires or when successfully dispelled.

spells.name: Phase Door

fields.Duration: One use per two caster levels

effect: Create an invisible passage through a wall that only the caster can see and use, disappearing on entry and reappearing on exit.
conditions: The inherited passwall materials are wood, plaster or stone.
exceptions: Dispel magic requires a higher-level magic-user, or cooperating lower-level casters whose total levels exceed twice the creator's level.

spells.name: Power Word, Stun
effect: Stun a target with 1–30 current HP for 4d4 rounds, 31–60 HP for 2d4 rounds, or 61–90 HP for 1d4 rounds.
conditions: The caster must face the chosen target.
Use current rather than maximum HP.
exceptions: A creature above 90 current HP is unaffected.

spells.name: Reverse Gravity

fields.Material: Lodestone and iron filings

effect: Reverse gravity so unfixed creatures and objects fall upward, then fall normally when the effect ends.
The paragraph's one-second example sends them 16 feet upward; hitting an overhead obstacle is resolved as a fall.
conditions: Objects already high in the air can be affected; the spell targets an area.
exceptions: Gap: the header gives one segment but the paragraph gives one second (one-sixth segment); the duration needs direct source/DM review.
Page 42 supports the seventh-level classification; page 88 supplies the spell mechanics.

spells.name: Simulacrum

fields.Material: Ice or snow, a piece of the original creature, and powdered ruby

effect: Form a duplicate with 51%–60% of the original's HP and 20%–50% of its level, if any.
Reincarnation supplies a vital force; limited wish supplies 40%–65% of the original's knowledge and personality.
conditions: It remains under its creator's command, given by ordinary communication rather than a special telepathic link.
exceptions: It cannot gain levels or improve its abilities.
Detect magic and true seeing reveal its nature; personality and knowledge differ from the original.

spells.name: Statue

fields.Material: Lime, sand and water stirred with an iron bar

effect: Turn into apparently solid stone while retaining normal sight, hearing and smell.
The initial change takes one full round; afterward the recipient can switch between statue and normal form in one-sixth segment for each change.
conditions: For initial survival, roll percentile, subtract Constitution and succeed on 82 or less; failure means system-shock death.
Damage to the stone body is still consequential, despite its hardness.
exceptions: A magical inspection detects a faint aura.

spells.name: Vanish
effect: Teleport an object weighing at most 500 gp per caster level, using teleport's procedure.
Heavier objects can instead vanish into the Ethereal Plane and be replaced with stone.
conditions: Both volume and the teleport weight limit matter.
The replacement stone is at least one foot thick or the original object's thickness, whichever is greater.
exceptions: A successful dispel magic returns an ethereally vanished item.

spells.name: Antipathy/Sympathy

fields.Area: One nonliving item or 10′ cube of area/level
fields.Material: Antipathy: alum soaked in vinegar; sympathy: 1,000 gp crushed pearls and honey

effect: Before casting, choose attraction or repulsion and a specific intelligent creature type or character alignment.
Antipathy forces failed savers away; a successful saver can remain but loses one Dexterity each round, to four lost points.
Sympathy compels failed savers to stay or retain the item. A successful saver must check again 1–6 turns later and returns if that save fails.
conditions: Name the specific creature kind or alignment rather than a broad group.
The spell cannot be placed on a living creature.
exceptions: Antipathy's avoidance lasts until the spell ends or is removed.

spells.name: Bigby's Clenched Fist

fields.Material: Leather glove and copper-zinc device of four joined rings on a bar

effect: Strike an opponent once each round without a to-hit roll; blow quality determines damage and possible stunning.
conditions: A stunned target adds +4 to the blow-quality roll.
No other spellcasting or magical activity is possible while controlling it.
exceptions: It withstands damage equal to its caster's HP and may be used with the other Bigby hand spells.
Blow roll: 1–12 deals 1d6; 13–16 deals 2d6; 17–19 deals 3d6 and stuns next round; 20 deals 4d6 and stuns for the next three rounds.

spells.name: Clone

fields.Material: Small piece of the person's flesh

effect: Grow a physical duplicate possessing the original's level, memories and knowledge as they stood when the flesh sample was taken.
conditions: Later experience and knowledge are absent; the original's equipment is not duplicated.
If both coexist, they know of one another and find the duplicate intolerable.
exceptions: Within a week, failure of one to destroy the other creates a 95% chance that one goes mad and destroys itself, with the clone selected 75% of the time; the remaining 5% outcome sends both mad and suicidal.

spells.name: Glassteel

fields.Area: One glass/crystal object, up to 10 pounds/level
fields.Material: Small pieces of glass and steel

effect: Turn glass or crystal into transparent material with steel's strength and resistance to breakage.
conditions: The affected material must be one whole object within the weight limit.

spells.name: Incendiary Cloud

fields.Saving throw: Half damage; successful save covers later exposure
fields.Area: Smoke cloud at least 10′ high and 20′ × 20′
fields.Material: Available fire source, scrapings from beneath dung, and pinch of dust

effect: Create dense smoke that burns on rounds three through five: ½ HP per caster level on rounds three and five, and one HP per caster level on round four.
Other rounds are obscuring but harmless smoke.
conditions: A creature that fails its first save retries on the later burning rounds as needed; one successful save suffices.
The smoke otherwise resembles pyrotechnics.

spells.name: Mass Charm

fields.Area: Up to 3″ × 3″; combined target HD/levels at most twice caster level

effect: Charm persons or monsters under the corresponding lower-level spell's rules, with a total HD/level budget of twice the caster's level.
conditions: Every target saves at −2 regardless of how many are selected.
All targets must be within range and the maximum area.
exceptions: Charm person checks for a new saving throw by Intelligence: 3 or less every 3 months; 4–6 every 2 months; 7–9 monthly; 10–12 every 3 weeks; 13–14 every 2 weeks; 15–16 weekly; 17 every 3 days; 18 every 2 days; 19 or more daily. Charm monster has a weekly chance to break by monster level or HD: 1st/up to 2, 5%; 2nd/up to 3+2, 10%; 3rd/up to 4+4, 15%; 4th/up to 6, 25%; 5th/up to 7+2, 35%; 6th/up to 8+4, 45%; 7th/up to 10, 60%; 8th/up to 12, 75%; 9th/over 12, 90%.

spells.name: Maze
effect: Trap the recipient in an extradimensional labyrinth until it finds its way out.
exceptions: Minotaurs are unaffected.
Time trapped by Intelligence: under 3, 2–8 turns; 3–5, 1–4 turns; 6–8, 5–20 rounds; 9–11, 4–16 rounds; 12–14, 3–12 rounds; 15–17, 2–8 rounds; 18 or more, 1–4 rounds.

spells.name: Mind Blank
effect: Protect against effects that read, detect or influence thoughts and emotions, including charm, fear, possession, feeblemind and soul trapping.
Hide the recipient from magical information gathering, including scrying, clairvoyance, communion and wish-based discovery.
exceptions: The protection also covers the listed psionic detection and influence powers.
Exceptionally powerful deities can penetrate it.

spells.name: Monster Summoning VI

fields.Material: Tiny bag and small candle, inherited from monster summoning I

effect: After 1–3 rounds, summon 1–2 sixth-level monsters selected by the referee.
conditions: Use the lesser spell's combat commands and communication-dependent service rules.

spells.name: Otto's Irresistible Dance
effect: Force the victim to dance instead of acting normally, worsen its AC by four, negate shield protection and prevent saving throws.
conditions: The caster must touch the victim, potentially requiring a melee-style attack.

spells.name: Permanency

fields.Area: Eligible personal, object or area spell

effect: Make an eligible spell permanent, paying one Constitution point per casting.
Personal options: comprehend languages, detect evil, detect invisibility, detect magic, infravision, protection from evil, protection from normal missiles, read magic, tongues and unseen servant.
Other listed options: enlarge, fear, gust of wind, invisibility, magic mouth, prismatic sphere, stinking cloud, wall of fire, wall of force and web.
conditions: For personal effects, cast the desired spell first, then permanency; these personal benefits cannot be bestowed on other creatures.
Nonliving targets allow simultaneous casting with the eligible effect.
exceptions: A personal application can be dispelled only by a higher-level magic-user than its creator was.
Other applications can be dispelled normally, ending the entire effect.
Gap: the header requires M but this paragraph names no material component.

spells.name: Polymorph Any Object

fields.Saving throw: Special; −4 when used as polymorph other or stone to flesh
fields.Material: Mercury, gum arabic and smoke

effect: Transform living or nonliving matter; duration depends on differences in kingdom, class, relationship, size, shape and Intelligence.
Closer transformations can be permanent; changing between kingdoms can shorten the result to hours or turns.
conditions: Living targets require system shock and retain the restrictions of the underlying polymorph/stone-to-flesh effects.
exceptions: The result radiates strong magic and reverts under dispel magic.

spells.name: Power Word, Blind

fields.Duration: 2–5 turns for ≤50 total HP; 2–5 rounds for 51–100 HP

effect: Blind chosen creatures, with duration determined by the combined HP affected.
conditions: Choose targets and the area center before resolving the spell.
exceptions: A creature above 100 HP is unaffected.
Cure blindness or dispel magic removes the blindness.

spells.name: Serten'S Spell Immunity

fields.Area: Up to one creature per four caster levels
fields.Material: Diamond crushed over recipients; each also carries an intact diamond of any size

effect: Grant saving-throw bonuses against the listed mental and control effects, including charm, suggestion, command, fear, hold, geas and quest.
conditions: Divide the total duration among recipients: the source's level-16 example gives one creature 16 turns, two eight turns each or four four turns each.
exceptions: Despite the name, the listed protection consists of saving-throw bonuses rather than blanket immunity.
Saving-throw bonuses: +9 versus beguiling, charm or suggestion; +7 versus command, domination, fear, hold or scare; +5 versus geas or quest.

spells.name: Symbol

fields.Area: Inscribed rune and its affected creatures
fields.Material: Powdered black opal and diamond dust, each worth at least 5,000 gp

effect: Choose a death, discord, fear, hopelessness, insanity, pain, sleep or stunning rune; each has its own target limits, saves and consequences.
The selected variant can kill, provoke conflict or panic, cause submission, induce confusion-like insanity, impair combat, or render victims asleep or stunned.
conditions: Triggering can involve reading, touching, passing over or crossing the inscribed portal.
A symbol cannot be identified by reading it without activating it.
exceptions: Death: one or more creatures totaling no more than 80 HP die. Discord: all argue for 5–20 rounds, with a 50% chance different alignments fight for 2–8 rounds. Fear: save at −4 or flee. Hopelessness: failed save imposes 3d4 turns of submission; each round 25% take no action, and of those acting 25% turn back or retire.

Insanity: one or more creatures totaling no more than 120 HP act as confused until healed by heal, restoration or wish. Pain: all suffer −2 Dexterity and −4 attacks for 2–20 turns. Sleep: creatures under 8+1 HD sleep for 1d12+4 turns. Stunning: one or more creatures totaling no more than 160 HP are stunned for 3d4 rounds and drop held items.

spells.name: Trap The Soul

fields.Saving throw: Special; spoken capture allows resistance and save
fields.Material: Gem worth 1,000 gp per victim HD/level, prepared with enchant an item and maze

effect: Imprison a creature's life force and body in the prepared gem.
conditions: The caster must see the creature and know its true name when completing the spell.
Speaking the final word in range allows magic resistance and a save; a successful save shatters the gem.
Alternatively, name a trigger object during preparation. The victim accepting that inscribed object is captured automatically; sympathy can encourage acceptance.
exceptions: Breaking the gem releases the victim and lets its body reform.
A powerful being trapped while away from its own plane can be required to perform a service on release; otherwise the freed creature is unconstrained.

spells.name: Astral Spell
